title: Business aviation support for aircraft owners
seoTitle: Aircraft Owner Services & Aviation Consulting | EXJET
description: Connect aircraft acquisitions, management, maintenance, interiors and connectivity with one ownership plan. Explore EXJET’s guides and discuss your aircraft.
kicker: For aircraft owners and family offices

sections.heading: Start with the decision in front of you
paragraphs: Buying an aircraft, changing management and planning a maintenance visit each require a different brief. EXJET helps owners, family offices and corporate aviation teams organize those decisions and coordinate the agreed consulting work.

Begin with the aircraft type, home base, expected use, project timing and the people authorized to approve changes. Define the deliverable before requesting competing proposals: a shortlist, an operating-budget comparison, a maintenance scope or a cabin-upgrade plan.

sections.heading: Match the service to the ownership stage
paragraphs: Use the same mission and timing assumptions across the teams involved. A lower acquisition price may come with near-term maintenance or cabin work; a planned refurbishment may affect the aircraft’s availability for travel.

sections.heading: Plan travel during aircraft downtime
paragraphs: Keep firm passenger commitments separate from a workshop’s estimated completion date. If supplemental charter is needed, brief the departure and arrival airports, passenger count, baggage and required timing early. Any proposed flight remains subject to operator acceptance, availability and a written quote.

sections.heading: Keep responsibilities clear
paragraphs: EXJET’s role and fees are defined in the consulting engagement. The appointed operator retains operational control; appropriately authorized maintenance providers perform and release technical work. Title, legal, tax and insurance decisions stay with the relevant professional advisers.

For a Dallas–Fort Worth aircraft, specify the actual base, such as Dallas Love Field or Addison, and any repositioning needs. The same planning process can be scoped for an aircraft based elsewhere. Do not send passenger identity documents or confidential ownership records until an appropriate exchange method is agreed.

faqs.question: Can an owner use EXJET for a single project?
faqs.answer: The engagement can focus on a defined decision or project, such as comparing management proposals or organizing a cabin-upgrade brief. Agree the scope, fees and responsibilities before work begins.

faqs.question: Does EXJET perform maintenance or operate my aircraft?
faqs.answer: EXJET provides consulting and coordination under the agreed scope. Operational control remains with the appointed operator, and technical work is performed and released by appropriately authorized providers.

title: Buying a business jet: an acquisition checklist
seoTitle: Buying a Business Jet: Aircraft Acquisition Checklist | EXJET
description: Build an aircraft acquisition brief, compare records and maintenance exposure, and plan inspection and delivery. Use EXJET’s buyer checklist to prepare your search.

sections.heading: Define the mission before the model
paragraphs: A useful acquisition brief describes the trips the aircraft must support. List the recurring city pairs, likely passenger and baggage loads, required arrival times, annual flying and home base. Separate routine missions from occasional longer trips so each candidate can be assessed consistently.

Manufacturer performance figures help form a shortlist. They do not establish the payload, range or runway capability of a particular aircraft on a particular day. Ask a qualified operational team to assess the intended missions using the aircraft’s actual configuration and applicable performance data.

links.label: Understand aircraft performance and specification assumptions

sections.heading: Build a comparable ownership picture
paragraphs: Use a common scope for every candidate. Record the asking price separately from transaction costs, immediate work and ongoing operating assumptions. Identify which amounts are documented, quoted or still estimates.

table.caption: Questions for the aircraft acquisition shortlist
rows: Aircraft identity
Registration, serial number, model and current configuration
Confirm the records and listing describe the same aircraft

Plan inspection scope and near-term downtime

Clarify coverage, exclusions and transfer costs

Define work required before entering service
Operating plan
Base, crew, hangar, insurance and management proposals
Estimate recurring costs on consistent assumptions

sections.heading: Separate technical review from title review
paragraphs: A pre-purchase inspection and a title review answer different questions. Agree the technical inspection scope with qualified specialists and the acceptance process with your advisers. Obtain the relevant aircraft records for independent review; a public registration search alone is not a complete title or technical assessment.

The FAA provides access to U.S. aircraft registration and airworthiness records. Confirm what has been obtained, what is missing and whether recent documents are still being processed. International transactions need a jurisdiction-specific plan from the appropriate advisers.

sections.heading: Set the acceptance and delivery process
paragraphs: Before committing to a schedule, identify who approves discrepancies, who pays for agreed rectification, how changes affect delivery and which documents must be provided. Coordinate escrow and closing instructions through independently verified channels with the appointed professionals.
bullets: Written representation, scope and fee arrangements.
Inspection facility, records access and technical review responsibilities.
Acceptance criteria and treatment of unresolved discrepancies.
Crew, insurance, hangar and management readiness for delivery.
Cabin or connectivity work scheduled against the first planned trip.

sections.heading: Treat archived listings as research
paragraphs: A historical listing can document how an aircraft was advertised at a point in time. It does not establish that the aircraft is currently available, that its specifications are unchanged or that EXJET represented a transaction. Request a current written specification and confirmation of availability for any aircraft under consideration.

links.label: View EXJET’s aircraft references and acquisition services

faqs.question: Is the purchase price the full cost of acquiring an aircraft?
faqs.answer: No. Define the transaction scope, inspection, immediate maintenance or upgrades, delivery arrangements and operating setup separately. Obtain aircraft-specific proposals rather than applying a generic allowance.

faqs.question: Does a registration record prove current charter authorization?
faqs.answer: No. Aircraft identity, ownership records, operator authority and aircraft authorization are separate checks. A registration record does not establish current charter availability.

title: How to compare aircraft management proposals
seoTitle: Aircraft Management Fees & Proposal Comparison | EXJET
description: Compare management fees, pass-through costs, crew coverage, charter-use assumptions and owner reporting. Prepare an aircraft management brief with EXJET.

sections.heading: Issue one brief to every provider
paragraphs: Compare proposals against the same aircraft, base, annual utilization and owner schedule. Include the expected domestic and international missions, passenger needs and any existing crew or hangar commitments. Otherwise a difference in the monthly fee may simply reflect a different scope.

Ask each provider to identify assumptions, exclusions and services supplied by third parties. An itemized first-year budget is easier to assess than a headline hourly cost that combines unrelated charges.

sections.heading: Look beyond the management fee
paragraphs: Separate recurring fixed expenses, flight-related costs and reserves or program payments. Request the method behind each estimate and the supporting invoice policy.

Set a consistent review cadence

sections.heading: Test charter-revenue assumptions separately
paragraphs: If charter use is being considered, request a separate scenario showing estimated gross revenue, owner proceeds, related costs, downtime and the effect on owner availability. Treat projected charter income as an assumption to evaluate, not a guaranteed offset to ownership costs.

Clarify the appointed operator, operational control, approval process and restrictions on use. The operator and the owner’s advisers need to review the actual arrangement; the management fee alone does not establish its suitability.

sections.heading: Make reporting useful to the owner
paragraphs: A family office may need expense allocation across households, while a corporate flight department may need reporting aligned to its internal approvals. Define who can authorize expenditure, which exceptions require escalation and how supporting records will be provided.

Ask for an example reporting format with confidential client information removed. Review how the provider explains variances from budget and forecasts upcoming maintenance, training and aircraft downtime.

sections.heading: Plan the first ninety days
paragraphs: Create a handover checklist for records, maintenance tracking, outstanding invoices, crew arrangements and travel already booked. Agree the responsible person for each item and the first budget review date. Resolve gaps before assuming the new arrangement is ready for service.

faqs.question: Can I compare providers using only the monthly management fee?
faqs.answer: The fee is only one part of the proposal. Compare included services, additional charges, purchasing arrangements, crew coverage, maintenance coordination and reporting on the same operating assumptions.

faqs.question: Will charter revenue cover the ownership cost?
faqs.answer: That cannot be assumed. Evaluate a documented aircraft-specific scenario, including charter-related costs, owner schedule priority, maintenance and demand. Forecast revenue is not a guarantee.

title: How to compare aircraft maintenance and MRO quotes
seoTitle: Aircraft Maintenance & MRO Quote Checklist | EXJET
description: Compare maintenance work scopes, exclusions, parts, change orders and downtime. Use EXJET’s MRO quote checklist to prepare an aircraft-specific project brief.

sections.heading: Give each provider the same work package
paragraphs: Start with the aircraft identity, current configuration, maintenance forecast and known discrepancies. Ask the responsible technical team to define the required work before comparing proposals. Identify mandatory tasks separately from optional improvements.

Include the location of the aircraft, any planned repositioning, the earliest induction date and the required return date. Do not describe an estimated workshop slot as a confirmed completion commitment.

sections.heading: Compare scope, not just the total
paragraphs: A fixed-price inspection quote may exclude findings, parts or additional access work. Request an itemized proposal that makes those boundaries visible.

table.caption: MRO proposal review checklist
rows: Scheduled tasks
Task references and included access or close-up work
Avoid different scopes being compared as equivalent
Labor
Fixed-price items, hourly work and overtime terms
Understand how additional work is priced

Availability, freight, exchange and core-return conditions
Identify supply and cost dependencies
Findings

Delivery
Work-completion records and release responsibilities
Agree what the owner receives at handover

sections.heading: Confirm provider capability for the actual work
paragraphs: Ask the technical team to verify that the proposed facility and personnel have the appropriate authority and capability for the aircraft and work scope. A general claim that a facility services business jets does not answer that aircraft-specific question.

EXJET coordinates the agreed consulting work. EXJET is not presented as the repair station, certifying engineer or party approving return to service. Those responsibilities remain with appropriately authorized providers.

sections.heading: Manage findings without losing cost control
paragraphs: Agree how findings will be documented, priced and approved. The owner’s representative should receive the impact on cost and schedule before authorizing additional work, with urgent airworthiness matters escalated to the responsible technical team.

For aircraft-on-ground support, communicate the known discrepancy and location to the qualified provider. Avoid promising a repair time before diagnosis, parts availability and the provider’s release requirements are known.

sections.heading: Plan downtime and the handover
paragraphs: Coordinate any cabin or connectivity work against the maintenance package. Shared access may make combined work worth considering, but engineering, parts or approval dependencies can also extend the visit. Ask for one coordinated schedule with clearly assigned owners.

Before delivery, review the agreed work-completion package, open items, invoices and remaining follow-up with the appointed technical representative. Arrange separate travel coverage for commitments that cannot move.

faqs.question: Does a maintenance quote cover all discrepancies found during inspection?
faqs.answer: Only if the written proposal expressly includes them. Ask how additional findings, parts, labor and schedule changes are authorized and charged.

faqs.question: Can EXJET guarantee a return-to-service date?
faqs.answer: A completion forecast depends on the qualified provider’s assessment, findings, parts and required approvals. Define the schedule and responsibilities in the project scope; do not treat an initial estimate as a guarantee.

title: Planning aircraft interiors and Starlink connectivity
seoTitle: Aircraft Interior Refurbishment & Starlink Planning | EXJET
description: Prepare a cabin refurbishment and connectivity brief. Review aircraft eligibility, installation scope, downtime and acceptance criteria with EXJET’s planning guide.

sections.heading: Describe how the cabin needs to work
paragraphs: Begin with the passenger experience: seating, sleeping arrangements, meetings, device charging, baggage and connectivity. Rank the changes by importance. Separate cosmetic refurbishment from changes that affect the cabin layout, installed equipment or aircraft configuration.

Provide the aircraft model, serial number, current equipment list and available modification records to the qualified technical team. A photograph or a model-family name alone cannot establish the engineering scope.

sections.heading: Confirm aircraft-specific eligibility first
paragraphs: For Starlink, verify current availability for the exact aircraft configuration with Starlink and the relevant approval holder or installation provider. A model listed as supported does not, by itself, confirm applicability to every serial number, configuration or registration jurisdiction.

The FAA describes a supplemental type certificate as approval for a change to an aeronautical product’s original design, including the change’s effect on that design. Ask the qualified provider to identify the applicable approval and installation requirements before committing to equipment or a slot.

sections.heading: Separate the project into comparable costs
paragraphs: Request separate scopes for interior work, engineering, connectivity equipment, installation and ongoing service. Confirm taxes, freight, additional findings and warranty terms in the written proposal. Do not assume a hardware price represents the installed project total.

sections.heading: Coordinate the visit with maintenance
paragraphs: Ask whether the upgrade can share a planned maintenance visit and whether combining the work creates additional dependencies. Set a decision date for materials and equipment, a change-order process and a reporting cadence.

Owners and family offices should identify who can approve design changes and extra expenditure. Corporate teams should confirm cabin-network and device requirements with their own IT advisers before finalizing the technical brief.

sections.heading: Agree the delivery evidence
paragraphs: Define the records, demonstrations and inspection needed for acceptance. Keep the agreed cabin appearance, installed functionality and technical release responsibilities distinct. Any promised performance should come from the current provider proposal and its stated conditions.

EXJET offers consulting and installation coordination within an agreed scope. EXJET is not represented as an authorized Starlink installer or certified repair station. Qualified providers carry out the technical work and associated approvals.

faqs.question: Can Starlink be installed on every business jet?
faqs.answer: Do not assume universal eligibility. Confirm the exact model, serial number, configuration, approval coverage and registration jurisdiction with the qualified provider using current information.

faqs.question: Is aircraft connectivity included in an interior refurbishment quote?
faqs.answer: Only when it is explicitly included. Separate equipment, installation, engineering, service plans and support in the written scope so proposals can be compared.
